messages:
Morgan: Kicking off a staged regional rollout for v2.3.1. Plan: US -> EU -> APAC. Pin US to v2.3.1 for 30m then reassess. Deploy-bot starting 10% slice in US now. Please watch capacity and error signals.

deploy-bot: RELEASE: v2.3.1 -> region=us slice=10% canaries=5 started by Morgan at 2026-03-21T18:00:00Z. Rollout policy: auto-progress if p99 latency and 5xx rate stable.

Aditya: quick question — are we routing to quantized variant in US or the full FP32? That affects GPU memory/thermal.

Morgan: routing to q4_0 for inference in US to keep cost down. Full FP32 fallback available on dedicated if we need it.

Sophie: seeing a small p95 bump on edge-us-3: baseline ~85ms -> 130ms on a handful of hosts. Not yet widespread. CPU/GPU util: 78%/65%. Tagging @ops.

Leo: running the smoke commands now:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"model":"v2.3.1","input":"smoke test"}' | jq .status
```
Logs: `smoke-req-1 -> 200, latency 110ms`, `smoke-req-2 -> 200, 125ms`. No 5xx so far.

Priya: Heads-up — EU capacity window is limited for the next 2hrs (maintenance). If US holds, we should delay EU progression until maintenance ends or we bump reserved pool. Recommend we keep EU pinned to v2.3.0 for now.

Aditya: proposed rollback criteria reminder: auto-rollback if 5xx rate >0.5% for 5m OR p99 latency > 2x baseline for 10m. Manual rollback threshold: product impact or customer reports.

Sophie: visualizing heatmap — small hotspot in us-east, but regional aggregate qps unchanged. I'm OK to let US stabilize for the 30m pin. Will re-check at +15m. :eyes:

Morgan: noted. I'm marking EU as "defer" in the rollout sheet and linking the release notes: https://internal/docs/releases/v2.3.1 (includes changelog, migration notes).

deploy-bot: UPDATE: us slice=10% -> monitor window started. Next auto-increase at +30m if no signals.

ops-bridge-bot: No active incidents in US. Alert thresholds running.

Leo: FYI did one load profile with burst=200rps for 2m against canaries — tail latency peaked at 210ms on 2 hosts, then recovered. Snapshot attached to the rollout doc.

Priya: If we see repeated 200ms spikes at our expected 150ms baseline, prefer to hold and increase canary size rather than progress. Also suggest increasing prefix cache TTL for common routes to reduce token cost and smoothing.

Aditya: Agree. Also we'll keep a pinned fallback route to v2.2.9 in the routing policy (pin-id: rollout-fallback-4788) so bridges can divert traffic if needed.

Sophie: +1. I'll set synthetic probes to run every 60s on the canary slice and post a short summary at +15m and +30m.

Morgan: thanks. If US is green at +30m we open EU to 10% and will manually unpin after EU reaches 10% and passes checks. APAC after EU +30m. Everyone stand by for +15m readout. :rocket:

Aditya: when unpinned, remember to update the console rollout notes (version pin history). small ops step but important for audits.

deploy-bot: NOTE: rollout metadata updated: pin=us:v2.3.1 expires=30m after 4788889999. Progress actions will post here.

Sophie: +15m check-in — p99 across US 118ms, 5xx 0.07%. No customer reports. Holding until +30m as planned.

Morgan: excellent. Leave EU deferred. If anything regresses, call for rollback and tag `#postmortems` if we hit the manual threshold.

Leo: copying the quick rollback command for convenience: `deploy-bot rollback --target-region us --to-version v2.2.9 --reason "auto/ops"`

Priya: noted. I'm increasing the reserved warm pool by 2 nodes for US as a precaution (will incur short-term cost).

ops-bridge-bot: Watchers added: Morgan, Sophie, Aditya, Leo, Priya. All clear for now.

Morgan: thanks everyone — will post final go/no-go at +30m. :thumbsup:
